sections.html:
A quitclaim deed transfers whatever interest the signer holds, and South Carolina treats it like other deeds for signing and recording. The deed must be proved or acknowledged before it can be recorded (SC Code 30-5-30), and quitclaim and non-warranty deeds are exempt from the derivation clause rule (30-5-35).

People use them to add a spouse, clear a name after divorce or move a house into a trust. Sellers sometimes ask whether one can stand in for a regular sale deed. It does move title. A buyer's title company, though, will take a close look.

The deed must be proved or acknowledged in one of the ways 30-5-30 allows, and the form in 27-7-10 contemplates two or more credible witnesses. The options are:

  • A subscribing witness swears an affidavit
  • The signing follows the Uniform Recognition of Acknowledgments Act, or the signer swears the signature is theirs
  • The grantor acknowledges the deed before an officer, with two witnesses present

A warranty clause is not required, and the form may carry other clauses the parties consider proper (27-7-20). A seal is not required if the attestation shows the parties meant the instrument to be sealed (27-7-30).

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed avoid the recording fee?
sections.html:
The exemption is narrow. A corrective or quitclaim deed that confirms title already vested in the grantee, with no consideration paid or to be paid, is exempt from the fee (SC Code 12-24-40(12)). If money changes hands, the exemption does not fit.

The ordinary fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value or fraction (12-24-10). The clerk or register must require an affidavit of value, and for an exempt deed the affidavit must give the reason for the exemption (12-24-70(A)(2)). A willfully false affidavit is a misdemeanor carrying a fine up to $1,000, up to a year in prison, or both (12-24-70(C)).

The exemption list in 12-24-40 is long. A few items come up in family and title situations.

TransferItem in 12-24-40
Realty valued at $100 or less(1)
Transfers where no gain or loss is recognized under IRC Section 1041(4)
Partition with no consideration beyond the interests exchanged(5)
Family partnership to partner, or family trust to beneficiary, where the only consideration is a reduced interest(9)
Corrective or quitclaim deeds confirming title already vested, with no consideration(12)
Deed in lieu of foreclosure or foreclosure deed to the mortgagee(13)

A transfer between spouses incident to divorce often falls under item 4, but the facts matter. Ask the register of deeds or clerk, or a South Carolina attorney.

The grantor is liable by default, jointly and severally if there are several, and the grantee is secondarily liable (12-24-20). For master-in-equity deeds and deeds from the federal government, a state or its subdivisions, the grantee is the liable party.

Whoever fails to pay can be penalized $50 to $500 for each failure, and a clerk who fails to collect faces that same range (12-24-120). The Department of Revenue may waive or reduce either penalty.

Survivorship depends on specific wording. A deed naming grantees followed by the words "as joint tenants with rights of survivorship, and not as tenants in common" creates a joint tenancy (27-7-40(a)). After a joint tenant dies, the survivor may file a certified death certificate with the register of deeds, and the filing is conclusive that the tenant is deceased (27-7-40(b)).

Divorce severs a husband-and-wife joint tenancy and leaves a tenancy in common without survivorship. If a quitclaim is meant to fix title after a death or divorce, work out which of these applies before you sign.

sections.h2: Using a quitclaim before a sale
sections.html:
A quitclaim works best for cleaning up who is on title before a sale, and less well as the sale deed itself. Common uses:

  • An heir who is not the personal representative releases an interest
  • An ex-spouse signs off after divorce
  • A co-owner transfers a share to the person selling

Title companies look at the whole chain, so a quitclaim in the chain may prompt questions. When an estate is involved, a deed of distribution from the personal representative is the usual instrument instead (62-3-907).

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is, even when the title is tangled. Send us what you have and we will tell you honestly whether the title needs work first.

Take it to the register of deeds in the county where the land sits. Counties outside the 30-5-10(A) list use the clerk of court instead. Deeds executed after July 1, 1976 need the grantee's mailing address (30-5-35). The register records instruments in the order lodged and within thirty days of lodgment (30-5-90).

Treat a quitclaim as final. The deed gives away your interest once it is delivered and recorded.

  • Confirm whether any money is changing hands, which decides whether the fee exemption applies
  • Get the signing witnessed by two people or arrange a subscribing witness affidavit (30-5-30)
  • Include the grantee's mailing address (30-5-35)
  • Prepare the affidavit stating the exemption reason if you claim one (12-24-70(A)(2))
  • Check for a mortgage, which a deed does not pay off

For a transfer into a trust or from a trust to its beneficiary, items 8 and 9 on the exemption list can matter. Moving property into a corporation, partnership or trust in exchange for an ownership interest, with no other consideration, is exempt, but transfers back out to the stockholder, partner or beneficiary are generally taxable (12-24-40(8)).

sections.h2: Other transfers the fee statute addresses
sections.html:
A few exemptions cover transfers that look like quitclaims but are different. Individual cemetery grave spaces sold by a cemetery company are exempt (12-24-40(6)), and so are contracts for the sale of timber to be cut (12-24-40(7)). Transfers to the federal government or to a state, its agencies and departments or political subdivisions, including school districts, are exempt too (12-24-40(2)).

For a house, the more relevant case is the corrective deed. If an earlier deed had a wrong legal description, a corrective deed confirming title already vested falls under item 12 when no consideration is paid.

sections.h2: Cost when the fee does apply
sections.html: If the exemption does not fit, the fee is the same $1.85 per $500 of value or fraction as on any other deed (12-24-10), split $1.30 state and $0.55 county (12-24-90). The grantor is liable by default (12-24-20), so the person giving up the interest may owe it. Ask the register's office to run the number from the stated value before you go in.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed valid in South Carolina?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is signed and proved or acknowledged as 30-5-30 requires and then recorded. It conveys the grantor's interest without needing a warranty clause (27-7-20).

faqs.q: Do I pay a recording fee on a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Not if it merely confirms title already vested in the grantee with no consideration (12-24-40(12)). You still file an affidavit stating the exemption reason.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed remove someone from a mortgage?
faqs.a: No. A deed does not pay off or release a loan, so talk to your lender. The deed and the loan are separate.

faqs.q: Can I use a quitclaim deed to sell my house?
faqs.a: You can record one, but buyers and title companies generally want to see the full chain of title. Ask a closing attorney which deed fits your sale.

faqs.q: Who pays if the fee applies?
faqs.a: The grantor by default, with the grantee secondarily liable (12-24-20).
